questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Agbabiaka LLP bought legal research software for N10,000,000 for use in its practice, expecting to use it for 10 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what capital allowance can Agbabiaka claim for 2026?
questions.explanation: The allowance is N10,000,000 x 25% = N2,500,000 for 2026, and the same amount in each following year while the software is used in the business. Option A spreads the cost over the 10-year expected use, option B uses the 20% rate, and option D uses 50%.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Agbabiaka LLP bought legal research software for N10,000,000 for use in its practice, expecting to use it for 10 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, why can't Agbabiaka simply deduct the N10,000,000 as an expense in computing its 2026 profit?

options.a: Relief is given only when the software is sold
options.b: Only manufacturing companies may claim relief for software
options.c: Software is never qualifying capital expenditure
options.d: Capital expenditure is not a deductible expense; it is recovered through capital allowances on qualifying capital expenditure

questions.explanation: Capital spending on an asset that lasts for years is not deductible like an ordinary expense; instead it is recovered gradually through capital allowances, and software is a recognised category of qualifying capital expenditure. Option C is wrong because software qualifies. Option B is wrong because any business using the asset for its trade can claim, and option A is wrong because relief is given annually while the asset is in use.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Mega Chicken Poultry Ltd bought poultry cages (agricultural equipment) for N10,000,000 for use on its poultry farm, expecting to use them for 10 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, at what annual rate is capital allowance claimed on agricultural equipment?
questions.explanation: Agricultural equipment is in the 20% class with plant, furniture and fittings, mining and other equipment. Option A is the rate for the separate agricultural expenditure category in the 10% class, not agricultural equipment. Option D is the rate for motor vehicles and software, and option B is not a class rate.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Mega Chicken Poultry Ltd bought poultry cages (agricultural equipment) for N10,000,000 for use on its poultry farm, expecting to use them for 10 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what annual capital allowance can Mega Chicken claim for 2026?
questions.explanation: At 20% of cost, the annual allowance is N10,000,000 x 20% = N2,000,000, claimed each year over about five years. Option A wrongly uses the 25% rate meant for software and motor vehicles. Option B uses 10%, and option D treats the whole cost as relieved in one year.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Mega Chicken Poultry Ltd bought poultry cages (agricultural equipment) for N10,000,000 for use on its poultry farm, expecting to use them for 10 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which capital allowance can Mega Chicken claim on the cages?

options.a: Only an annual allowance at a fixed rate on cost; there is no initial allowance
options.b: An allowance only in the year the cages are sold
options.c: Nothing, because agricultural assets are outside capital allowances
options.d: An initial allowance in 2026 plus an annual allowance on the balance

questions.explanation: Since 1 January 2026, the only capital allowance is the annual allowance at fixed rates on original cost; the old initial allowance and balancing adjustments are gone. Option D describes the old regime. Option C is wrong because agricultural equipment is a qualifying category, and option B confuses allowances with relief on disposal.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Gold Miners Ltd bought mining cranes for N10,000,000 for use in its mining operations, expecting to use them for 5 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, at what annual rate is capital allowance claimed on the cranes?
questions.explanation: Mining expenditure and plant are in the 20% class, so the cranes qualify at 20% of cost each year. Option D is for buildings, agricultural expenditure, masts, intangibles and heavy transportation. Option B is for motor vehicles and software, and option C is not a class rate.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Gold Miners Ltd bought mining cranes for N10,000,000 for use in its mining operations, expecting to use them for 5 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what capital allowance can Gold Miners claim for 2026?
questions.explanation: The allowance is N10,000,000 x 20% = N2,000,000 a year while the cranes are used in the business. Option C uses 25%, option B uses 10%, and option A uses 50%.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Gold Miners Ltd bought mining cranes for N10,000,000 for use in its mining operations, expecting to use them for 5 years. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which of these would stop the cranes from counting as qualifying capital expenditure?

options.a: The cranes are used by the company's own staff
options.b: The company is a mining company rather than a manufacturer
options.c: The cranes were imported but the import duties on them were not paid
options.d: The cranes were bought at the start of the year rather than at the end

questions.explanation: An imported asset whose import duties have not been paid does not qualify for capital allowances, in the same way that an asset on which VAT was due but not paid does not qualify. Option A is normal business use and does not disqualify the asset. Options D and B are irrelevant, because the asset only needs to be owned and used for the business at the end of the basis period.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, a commercial bank bought a staff bus for N100,000,000, treated as motor vehicle expenditure under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. For 2026 its gross income was N500,000,000 and its allowable expenses (salaries, operating costs) were N200,000,000. It also carries N100,000,000 of tax overpaid for 2025 that has not been refunded. Company income tax is 30%; ignore the development levy and any minimum tax. What capital allowance can the bank claim on the bus for 2026?
questions.explanation: Motor vehicles are in the 25% class, so the allowance is N100,000,000 x 25% = N25,000,000 for 2026. Option A spreads the cost over the bank's own 10-year estimate (10%), option D uses the 20% equipment rate, and option B treats the whole cost as deductible at once.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, a commercial bank bought a staff bus for N100,000,000, treated as motor vehicle expenditure under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. For 2026 its gross income was N500,000,000 and its allowable expenses (salaries, operating costs) were N200,000,000. It also carries N100,000,000 of tax overpaid for 2025 that has not been refunded. Company income tax is 30%; ignore the development levy and any minimum tax. What is the bank's total (taxable) profit for 2026?
questions.explanation: Adjusted profit is N500,000,000 - N200,000,000 = N300,000,000, and deducting the N25,000,000 capital allowance gives total profit of N275,000,000. Option C wrongly deducts the overpaid tax from profit; overpaid tax is a credit against tax payable, not an expense. Option B ignores the capital allowance, and option A deducts the full cost of the bus.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, a commercial bank bought a staff bus for N100,000,000, treated as motor vehicle expenditure under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. For 2026 its gross income was N500,000,000 and its allowable expenses (salaries, operating costs) were N200,000,000. It also carries N100,000,000 of tax overpaid for 2025 that has not been refunded. Company income tax is 30%; ignore the development levy and any minimum tax. How does the N100,000,000 overpaid tax affect the bank's 2026 company income tax?

options.a: Tax of N52,500,000 (30% of N175,000,000) is payable in cash
options.b: Tax of N82,500,000 (30% of N275,000,000) is covered by setting off the overpaid tax, leaving N17,500,000 still due to the bank
options.c: Tax of N82,500,000 is payable in cash, and the overpaid tax can only be refunded separately
options.d: No tax arises because banks are exempt

questions.explanation: Company income tax is 30% x N275,000,000 = N82,500,000, and unrefunded overpaid tax can be set off against this liability, so nothing is payable and N17,500,000 remains for refund or future set-off. Option A comes from wrongly deducting the overpaid tax from profit. Option C ignores the set-off, and option D is wrong because banks are taxable companies.

questions.question: Why does the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 grant capital allowances to companies?

options.a: To replace the companies income tax charge on manufacturing companies
options.b: To refund the VAT that companies paid when buying fixed assets
options.c: Because capital expenditure is not deductible in computing profits, so allowances give relief for it
options.d: Because depreciation charged in the accounts is fully deductible anyway

questions.explanation: Capital expenditure cannot be deducted as an expense, so the Act lets companies recover qualifying capital expenditure through capital allowances. Option D is wrong because accounting depreciation is not deductible, and Option B confuses capital allowances with input VAT.

questions.question: Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, capital expenditure on assets such as plant, buildings, software and motor vehicles that can attract capital allowances is called:
questions.explanation: Expenditure on qualifying categories of assets is called Qualifying Capital Expenditure, and capital allowances are claimed on it. Option C refers to revenue expenses deducted directly, which cannot also be QCE, and Option B is a profit figure, not a type of expenditure.

questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which condition must an asset meet for a company to claim capital allowance on it for a basis period?

options.a: It must have been held for at least five years
options.b: It must have been depreciated in the accounts at the same rate
options.c: It must have been bought with cash rather than on credit
options.d: It must be owned and in use for the business at the end of the basis period

questions.explanation: Capital allowance is available where the asset is owned and used for business purposes at the end of the relevant basis period. Option B is wrong because tax rates do not depend on accounting depreciation, and Option A invents a holding period.

questions.question: Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what annual capital allowance rate applies to building expenditure?
questions.explanation: Building expenditure falls in Class 1, which carries an annual allowance of 10% of cost. Option A is the Class 2 rate for plant and equipment, and Option C is the Class 3 rate for motor vehicles and software.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Class 1 (10%) item under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?
questions.explanation: Class 1 at 10% covers building, agricultural, mast, intangible asset and heavy transportation expenditure. Options B and C are Class 2 at 20%, and Option A is Class 3 at 25%.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Class 2 (20%) item under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?
questions.explanation: Class 2 at 20% covers plant, furniture and fittings, agricultural equipment, mining and other equipment; software is in Class 3 at 25%. Options A, B and D are genuine Class 2 items.

questions.question: Which group correctly lists the Class 3 (25%) items under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?

options.b: Agricultural equipment, motor vehicles and buildings
options.d: Motor vehicles, software and other capital expenditure

questions.explanation: Class 3 carries the highest rate of 25% and covers motor vehicle, software and other capital expenditure. Option C lists Class 1 items at 10%, and Option A lists Class 2 items at 20%.

questions.question: Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what annual capital allowance rate applies to furniture and fittings expenditure?
questions.explanation: Furniture and fittings are in Class 2, which attracts 20% a year on cost. Option C is the Class 1 rate for buildings, and Option A is the Class 3 rate for motor vehicles and software.

questions.question: Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, intangible asset expenditure attracts capital allowance at:
questions.explanation: Intangible asset expenditure is listed in Class 1 with buildings, masts and heavy transportation, at 10% a year. Option D is the software rate, which students often confuse with intangibles, and Option B is wrong because intangibles are expressly a qualifying category.

questions.question: How does the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 treat 'agricultural expenditure' compared with 'agricultural equipment expenditure'?

options.a: Both are treated as Class 1 expenditure at 10% a year
options.b: Both are treated as Class 2 expenditure at 20% a year
options.c: Agricultural expenditure is Class 3 at 25%, while agricultural equipment is Class 1 at 10%
options.d: Agricultural expenditure is Class 1 at 10%, while agricultural equipment expenditure is Class 2 at 20%

questions.explanation: The Act separates agricultural expenditure (Class 1, 10%) from agricultural equipment expenditure (Class 2, 20%). Options A and B merge the two categories, which the Schedule keeps apart.

questions.question: Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, mining expenditure attracts capital allowance at:
questions.explanation: Mining expenditure is a Class 2 item at 20% of cost each year. Option A is the Class 1 rate, and Option B reflects the kind of large first-year initial allowance that no longer exists.

questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how is the annual capital allowance on qualifying capital expenditure computed?

options.a: As an initial allowance in year one plus annual allowance on the residue
options.b: At a fixed class rate on the original cost every year until the cost is fully recovered
options.c: At the same rate the company uses for depreciation in its accounts
options.d: At a fixed rate on the reducing (written-down) balance each year

questions.explanation: The Act applies fixed annual rates to the original cost of the asset, the same amount each year, until the full value is recovered. Option D describes reducing balance, and Option A describes the old initial-plus-annual approach.

questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what initial allowance is available on qualifying capital expenditure incurred from 1 January 2026?

options.a: 50% of cost in the first year
options.b: None, because the initial allowance has been abolished
options.c: An amount equal to the first annual allowance
options.d: 25% of cost in the first year

questions.explanation: The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 removed the initial allowance, so the annual allowance is the only capital allowance available. Options A and D describe the type of first-year relief that existed under the old regime.

questions.question: Ibadan Plastics Ltd bought a machine on which VAT was due but was not paid. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, can it claim capital allowance on the machine?

options.a: No, because an asset on which VAT applies and is not paid does not qualify as QCE
options.b: Yes, once it pays a penalty equal to the VAT
options.c: Yes, in full, because VAT is irrelevant to capital allowances
options.d: Yes, but only at half the normal rate

questions.explanation: An asset on which VAT applies but has not been paid is not qualifying capital expenditure, so no allowance is due. Option C ignores this condition, and Options B and D invent partial or penalty-based relief.

questions.question: Kaduna Textiles Ltd imported a loom but has not paid the import duty on it. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how is the loom treated for capital allowance?

options.a: It is not eligible QCE until the import duty is paid
options.b: It qualifies at 10% because duty is unpaid
options.c: It qualifies, and the unpaid duty is added to its cost
options.d: It qualifies at 20% because it is plant

questions.explanation: An imported asset whose import duties are not paid is not eligible qualifying capital expenditure. Option D gives the normal Class 2 rate without applying the duty condition, and Option C rewards non-payment by inflating the cost.

questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how is capital allowance treated on an asset used partly to earn income that is not assessable to tax?

options.a: It is always claimed in full, whatever the mix of income
options.b: It is disallowed completely for the whole asset
options.c: It is prorated only where non-assessable income exceeds 50% of total income
options.d: It is prorated to the assessable part, unless non-assessable income is below 10% of total income

questions.explanation: Where an asset serves both assessable and non-assessable income, the allowance is apportioned, except where the non-assessable income is less than 10% of total income. Option A ignores the proration rule, and Option C uses the wrong threshold.

questions.question: Abeokuta Pharma Ltd holds an Economic Development Tax Incentive certificate for a priority product and also runs a non-priority business. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, against which profits can the capital allowance attributable to its priority activities be deducted?

options.a: No profits, because incentive companies cannot claim capital allowance at all
options.b: Any profits of the company, at its choice
options.c: Only the assessable profit of the priority business
options.d: Only the profits of the non-priority business

questions.explanation: Capital allowance attributable to the priority activities of a company enjoying the incentive is deductible only from the assessable profit of the priority business. Options B and D would let the company shelter non-priority profits with priority allowances, which the rule prevents.

questions.question: A company deducted the cost of an item as an allowable business expense in computing its profit. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, can it also treat that cost as QCE?

options.a: Yes, but at half the normal capital allowance rate
options.b: Yes, a company may claim both a deduction and a capital allowance
options.c: Yes, but only if the item costs more than N1 million
options.d: No, because expenditure allowed as a deductible expense does not qualify as QCE

questions.explanation: Expenditure already allowed as a deductible expense cannot also be qualifying capital expenditure, so there is no double relief. Option B would give relief twice for the same cost, and Options A and C invent conditions.

questions.question: A company bought a foreign machine using foreign exchange obtained at a rate above the official exchange rate. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how much of the cost is QCE?

options.a: The cost at the official rate plus half of the excess
options.b: The full naira amount actually paid
options.c: Only the cost at the official exchange rate; the excess is excluded
options.d: Nothing, because the purchase is disqualified

questions.explanation: Any amount above the official exchange rate incurred to acquire a capital asset is left out of qualifying capital expenditure. Option B would include the premium, and Option D goes too far because the asset still qualifies at the official rate.

questions.question: Under the old Companies Income Tax Act, N10 was retained in the books for each asset until disposal. What is retained under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?

options.a: N10 for each asset, exactly as under the old law
options.b: 1% of the qualifying capital expenditure, as a notional amount only
options.c: 10% of the cost, which reduces the allowance claimable
options.d: Nothing at all; no amount is retained in the books

questions.explanation: The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 replaces the N10 retention with 1% of the qualifying capital expenditure, kept as a notional figure until disposal. Option A is the old rule, and Option C confuses the retention with the Class 1 rate and wrongly says it affects claims.

questions.question: Under the old Companies Income Tax Act, capital allowances claimable by many companies were restricted to a fraction of assessable profits. What is the position under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?

options.a: The restriction no longer applies, so the full annual allowance can be claimed
options.b: Allowances are now restricted to one-half of assessable profits
options.c: Allowances can only be claimed in years with no losses
options.d: The two-thirds restriction now applies to all companies, including manufacturers

questions.explanation: The former two-thirds restriction on capital allowances has been removed, so companies can claim the full allowance. Options B and D impose limits the new Act does not contain.

questions.question: Bello & Partners, a law firm, bought legal research software for its practice. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which rate of capital allowance applies?

options.b: No allowance, because professional firms cannot claim

questions.explanation: Software expenditure is a Class 3 item at 25% a year. Option D treats the software as a general intangible asset, but the Schedule lists software separately in Class 3, and Option B is wrong because a firm using the asset for its business can claim.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a condition or rule for capital allowances under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?

options.a: Import duties on an imported asset must have been paid
options.b: Any foreign exchange cost above the official rate is excluded from QCE
options.c: An initial allowance must be claimed before any annual allowance
options.d: VAT due on the asset must have been paid

questions.explanation: There is no initial allowance under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, so it cannot be a condition. Options A, B and D are all genuine rules on what counts as qualifying capital expenditure.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Ajah Consulting Ltd bought accounting software for N12,000,000 and uses it in its business. Under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (software: 25% a year on cost), what is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Annual allowance = 25% x N12,000,000 = N3,000,000, the same each year. Option D uses the Class 2 rate, and Option A applies 25% to a reduced balance, which the fixed-rate-on-cost method does not do.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026, Ogun Poultry Ltd bought poultry cages for N15,000,000. The cages are classified as agricultural equipment expenditure (Class 2, 20% a year on cost) under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. What is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Annual allowance = 20% x N15,000,000 = N3,000,000, the same each year until the cost is recovered. Option B applies 25%, the rate for motor vehicles and software, and Option C uses the 10% rate meant for agricultural expenditure such as plantations rather than equipment.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026 a company bought equipment classified as agricultural equipment expenditure (20% a year on cost) under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, for N8,000,000, expecting to use it for 10 years. Over how many years will the cost be recovered, and in which year is the last allowance claimed?

options.a: 5 years; the last allowance is claimed for 2031
options.b: 5 years; the last allowance is claimed for 2030
options.c: 4 years; the last allowance is claimed for 2029
options.d: 10 years; the last allowance is claimed for 2035

questions.explanation: At 20% a year on cost, the allowance is N1,600,000 a year and the cost is recovered in 100/20 = 5 years: 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030. Option C uses a 25% rate, and Option D follows the asset's useful life instead of the statutory rate.

questions.question: A factory building cost N80,000,000 on 1 January 2026. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (buildings: 10% a year on cost), what is its tax written-down value after the allowances for 2026, 2027 and 2028?
questions.explanation: Allowance = 10% x N80,000,000 = N8,000,000 a year; after 3 years: N80,000,000 - 3 x N8,000,000 = N56,000,000. Option C applies 10% on the reducing balance, and Option A deducts only one year.

questions.question: Plant costing N45,000,000 was bought on 1 January 2026. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (plant: 20% a year on cost), what are the total capital allowances claimed for 2026 and 2027 together?
questions.explanation: Each year: 20% x N45,000,000 = N9,000,000; two years = N18,000,000. Option A uses the reducing balance in the second year, and Option D uses the 25% rate.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026 Asaba Foods Ltd acquired: a building N100,000,000, plant N40,000,000, a motor vehicle N16,000,000 and software N8,000,000. Using the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 rates (buildings 10%; plant 20%; motor vehicles and software 25%; all on cost), what is the total capital allowance for 2026?
questions.explanation: Building N10,000,000 + plant N8,000,000 + vehicle N4,000,000 + software N2,000,000 = N24,000,000. Option C applies a single 20% rate to everything, and Option D treats software as a 10% intangible.

questions.question: A company bought a motor vehicle for N20,000,000 (25% a year on cost under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025). It uses the vehicle for both activities, and 30% of the company's total income is not assessable to tax. What capital allowance can it deduct for the year?
questions.explanation: Full allowance = 25% x N20,000,000 = N5,000,000; non-assessable income is 30% (not below 10%), so prorate: N5,000,000 x 70% = N3,500,000. Option B ignores proration, and Option D keeps the non-assessable share instead of the assessable share.

questions.question: Jos Mills Ltd has plant costing N30,000,000 (20% a year on cost under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025) used for all its activities. Its total income is N150,000,000, of which N12,000,000 is not assessable. What capital allowance can it claim?
questions.explanation: Non-assessable income = N12,000,000/N150,000,000 = 8%, which is less than 10%, so no proration: allowance = 20% x N30,000,000 = N6,000,000. Option A prorates even though the 10% exception applies.

questions.question: Plant costing N50,000,000 (20% a year on cost under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025) is used for all of a company's activities. Total income is N200,000,000, of which N40,000,000 is not assessable. What capital allowance is deductible?
questions.explanation: Non-assessable share = 20%, which is not below 10%, so prorate: 20% x N50,000,000 = N10,000,000, x 80% = N8,000,000. Option C ignores proration, and Option A wrongly cuts the allowance by a flat 10%.

questions.question: A company bought an imported machine for $10,000. It paid N1,700 per dollar, but the official exchange rate was N1,500 per dollar. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (plant: 20% a year on cost, excess over official rate excluded from QCE), what is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: QCE = $10,000 x N1,500 = N15,000,000 (the excess N2,000,000 is excluded); allowance = 20% x N15,000,000 = N3,000,000. Option B includes the premium paid above the official rate.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026 a company bought: plant N24,000,000 (VAT paid), furniture N18,000,000 (VAT due but not paid) and other equipment N6,000,000 (VAT paid). All are Class 2 (20% on cost) under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. What is the total capital allowance for 2026?
questions.explanation: The furniture is not QCE because VAT due on it was not paid; allowance = 20% x (N24,000,000 + N6,000,000) = N6,000,000. Option D includes the furniture, and Option A wrongly drops the other equipment too.

questions.question: A company imported two machines (Class 2, 20% on cost under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025): Machine A cost N60,000,000 with import duty paid, and Machine B cost N25,000,000 with import duty unpaid. What capital allowance can it claim for the year?
questions.explanation: Only Machine A is eligible QCE: 20% x N60,000,000 = N12,000,000. Machine B is excluded because its import duty is unpaid. Option C includes Machine B, and Option D wrongly nets one cost against the other.

questions.question: Warri Logistics Ltd (not a small company) has gross income of N400,000,000 and allowable operating expenses of N150,000,000 for 2026. On 1 January 2026 it bought a motor vehicle for N40,000,000 (25% a year on cost under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025). What is its taxable profit after capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Adjusted profit = N400,000,000 - N150,000,000 = N250,000,000; capital allowance = 25% x N40,000,000 = N10,000,000; taxable profit = N240,000,000. Option B deducts the full cost of the vehicle, which is a capital expense, and Option C uses 10%.

questions.question: Using the Warri Logistics Ltd figures (adjusted profit N250,000,000, capital allowance N10,000,000), what is its companies income tax at 30% under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?
questions.explanation: Taxable profit = N250,000,000 - N10,000,000 = N240,000,000; tax = 30% x N240,000,000 = N72,000,000. Option C ignores the capital allowance, and Option B deducts the full vehicle cost.

questions.question: For 2026 a bank (not a small company) has adjusted profit of N300,000,000 and capital allowance of N25,000,000. It also has N50,000,000 of overpaid tax from 2025 that is available as a credit against its 2026 tax. With companies income tax at 30% under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what tax remains payable for 2026?
questions.explanation: Taxable profit = N300,000,000 - N25,000,000 = N275,000,000; tax = 30% = N82,500,000; less the N50,000,000 tax credit = N32,500,000. Option D wrongly deducts the overpaid tax from profit before applying 30%; a tax credit reduces tax, not profit.

questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a company had been claiming capital allowances on an item of plant under the old Companies Income Tax Act for 3 years. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 plant is written off at 20% a year (5 years). If the transitional rule gives remaining years equal to the new period less the years already claimed, how many more years of allowance remain?
questions.explanation: Remaining years = years under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (100/20 = 5) - years already claimed (3) = 2 years. Option B ignores the years already claimed, and Option C repeats the years already claimed.

questions.question: A warehouse was bought on 1 January 2026 and qualifies as building expenditure (10% a year on cost) under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. If allowances are claimed every year from 2026, for which year is the final allowance claimed?
questions.explanation: At 10% a year, the cost is recovered over 100/10 = 10 years, from 2026 to 2035 inclusive. Option A counts one year too many, and Option C uses the 20% (5-year) rate.

questions.question: A company claims an annual capital allowance of N2,400,000 on an asset costing N12,000,000, the same amount each year, under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. Which class and rate does the asset fall into?
questions.explanation: Rate = N2,400,000 / N12,000,000 = 20%, which is the Class 2 rate covering plant, furniture, agricultural equipment, mining and other equipment. Option C attaches the wrong rate to Class 2.

questions.question: A telecom company erected a mast for N60,000,000. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 First Schedule (mast expenditure: 10% a year on cost), what is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Annual allowance = 10% x N60,000,000 = N6,000,000. Option D treats the mast as plant at 20%, and Option C applies 10% to a reduced balance.

questions.question: A company acquired a patent (an intangible asset) for N25,000,000. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (intangible assets: 10% a year on cost), what is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Annual allowance = 10% x N25,000,000 = N2,500,000. Option D uses the 25% software rate, and Option A writes off the whole cost at once, which the Act does not allow.

questions.question: A hotel bought furniture and fittings for N7,500,000. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (furniture and fittings: 20% a year on cost), what is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Annual allowance = 20% x N7,500,000 = N1,500,000. Option B uses the Class 3 rate, and Option C uses the Class 1 rate.

questions.question: A shipping company incurred N500,000,000 classified as heavy transportation expenditure under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (10% a year on cost). What is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Annual allowance = 10% x N500,000,000 = N50,000,000. Option C treats it as an ordinary motor vehicle at 25%, but heavy transportation is a Class 1 item.

questions.question: A company incurred N4,000,000 classified as 'other capital expenditure' under the First Schedule to the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (25% a year on cost). What is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: Other capital expenditure is in Class 3: 25% x N4,000,000 = N1,000,000. Option B confuses it with 'other equipment', which is Class 2 at 20%.

questions.question: A saloon car (motor vehicle expenditure) cost N30,000,000 on 1 January 2026. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (25% a year on cost), what is its tax written-down value after the 2026 and 2027 allowances?
questions.explanation: Allowance = 25% x N30,000,000 = N7,500,000 a year; after 2 years: N30,000,000 - N15,000,000 = N15,000,000. Option A uses the reducing-balance method.

questions.question: An asset with qualifying capital expenditure of N50,000,000 is held by a company. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what amount must be retained in the books as a notional value until disposal?
questions.explanation: The retention is 1% of qualifying capital expenditure: 1% x N50,000,000 = N500,000. Option A is the old N10 retention, and Option C confuses the retention with the 10% Class 1 rate.

questions.question: Gold Diggers Ltd bought mining cranes for N36,000,000 on 1 January 2026, classified as mining expenditure (20% a year on cost) under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. What is the cumulative capital allowance claimed by the end of 2028?
questions.explanation: Annual allowance = 20% x N36,000,000 = N7,200,000; for 2026, 2027 and 2028: 3 x N7,200,000 = N21,600,000. Option B counts only two years, and Option D uses 25%.

questions.question: Software bought on 1 January 2026 is written off at 25% a year on cost under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. After the allowances for 2026, 2027 and 2028 have been claimed, how many years of allowance remain?
questions.explanation: At 25% a year, software is recovered over 100/25 = 4 years (2026-2029). After 3 years, 4 - 3 = 1 year remains. Option C assumes a 10-year write-off, and Option D forgets the 2029 claim.

questions.question: On 1 January 2026 a company bought plant for N40,000,000 (20% on cost) and a building for N120,000,000 (10% on cost) under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. What are the total capital allowances claimed on both assets for 2026, 2027 and 2028 combined?
questions.explanation: Annual total = 20% x N40,000,000 + 10% x N120,000,000 = N8,000,000 + N12,000,000 = N20,000,000; over 3 years = N60,000,000. Option D is one year only, and Option C swaps the two rates.

questions.question: Ikoyi Chambers LLP bought legal research software on 1 January 2026 for N18,000,000, expecting to use it for 10 years. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (software: 25% a year on cost), what is the annual capital allowance?
questions.explanation: The statutory rate, not the expected life, decides the allowance: 25% x N18,000,000 = N4,500,000 a year for 4 years. Option C spreads the cost over the 10-year expected life (in effect a 10% rate), and Option D writes off the whole cost at once, which the fixed annual rates do not allow.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what does the Economic Development Tax Incentive give a company operating in a designated priority sector?

options.a: A tax credit of 5% per annum of its qualifying capital expenditure, for an initial period of five years
options.b: An initial allowance of 50% on all its qualifying capital expenditure in the first year
options.c: An exemption from charging VAT on all its sales for ten years
options.d: A full income tax holiday of three years, extendable by two years

questions.explanation: The Economic Development Tax Incentive works as a tax credit: a priority-sector company earns a credit of 5% of each qualifying capital expenditure every year for an initial five years and uses it to offset tax on profits from its priority products. Option D describes the old pioneer status tax holiday, which this incentive replaced. Option B is wrong because initial allowances no longer exist under the 2025 framework, and option C is not part of the incentive.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: The Economic Development Tax Incentive under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 replaced which earlier incentive for companies in priority industries?

options.a: Pioneer status (the income tax holiday for pioneer industries)

questions.explanation: Pioneer status used to give approved companies an income tax holiday; the 2025 reform replaced it with a credit-based Economic Development Tax Incentive tied to qualifying capital expenditure. Option D is a separate regime that still exists for licensed zone entities, and option B is a separate relief for companies under the small company thresholds. Option C has nothing to do with priority-sector incentives.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: A company holding an Economic Development Tax Incentive certificate under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 wants its initial five-year incentive period extended by a further five years. What condition must it meet?

options.a: It must reinvest 100% of its profits from the incentive period in expanding the same product(s)
options.b: It must employ at least 1,000 Nigerian staff
options.c: It must list its shares on the Nigerian Exchange
options.d: It must export at least 75% of its output

questions.explanation: The extension for another five years is a reward for full reinvestment: the company must plough 100% of its profits from the incentive period back into expanding the same products. Option D sounds like the free trade zone sales test, which is a different regime. Options B and C are not conditions for the extension.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, until 31 December 2027 a free trade zone entity keeps its full tax exemption provided that its sales to the Nigerian customs territory do not exceed what share of its total sales?
questions.explanation: A free zone entity stays fully exempt where its sales come from exports (or inputs for exports) and not more than 25% of its sales go into the Nigerian customs territory; above that, its profits on sales to the customs territory become taxable. Option D mixes this up with the other side of the same test, since at least 75% of sales must be for export. Options C and A are not the statutory threshold.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what changes for free trade zone entities from 1 January 2028, unless the date is extended by Presidential order?

options.a: They may sell up to 50% of their output in the customs territory tax-free
options.b: They pay a flat 2% levy on turnover instead of income tax
options.c: Their profits from exports also become fully taxable
options.d: Their profits from sales to the Nigerian customs territory become fully taxable, whatever the percentage of such sales

questions.explanation: From 1 January 2028 the 25% cushion disappears: any sales into the customs territory are fully taxable, even small ones, although the President may defer this date by order. Option C is wrong because export-related profits keep their exemption. Options A and B are not provisions of the Act.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a 'small company' that pays company income tax at 0% is one whose

options.a: annual gross turnover is N50,000,000 or less and total fixed assets do not exceed N100,000,000
options.b: annual gross turnover is N100,000,000 or less and total fixed assets do not exceed N250,000,000 (professional service providers excluded)
options.c: annual gross turnover is N25,000,000 or less, with no fixed asset test
options.d: assessable profit is N100,000,000 or less, whatever its turnover

questions.explanation: Small company status under the 2025 Acts uses two tests together: gross turnover of N100,000,000 or less and fixed assets not above N250,000,000, with businesses providing professional services excluded. Such companies pay 0% company income tax and are also outside the development levy. Option C reflects the old, much lower turnover threshold, and option D wrongly uses profit instead of turnover.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, companies engaged in primary agricultural businesses such as crop production, livestock or dairy farming enjoy an income tax exemption for

options.a: as long as they reinvest all their profits
options.b: their first two years of operation
options.c: their first five years of operation
options.d: their first ten years of operation

questions.explanation: The 2025 Acts give new agricultural businesses in primary production an initial tax-free period of five years to encourage investment in food production. Options B and D give the wrong length of the period. Option A borrows the reinvestment idea from the Economic Development Tax Incentive extension, which is a different incentive.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the profits of a licensed free trade zone or export processing zone entity are fully exempt from tax where:

options.a: Its sales are wholly for export, or not more than 25% of its sales go to the customs territory
options.b: It is owned 100% by Nigerian shareholders resident in Nigeria
options.c: It sells at least 25% of its output in the Nigerian customs territory
options.d: It employs at least 25 Nigerian staff in its zone operations

questions.explanation: Full exemption applies where the entity's sales come from exports, or from inputs into goods or services exclusively meant for export, or where no more than 25% of its total sales go to the customs territory. Option C reverses the test, and Options B and D are not conditions in the Act.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In the free trade zone rules of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what does the 'customs territory' refer to?

options.a: The fenced area inside a licensed free trade zone
options.b: Only the seaports and airports through which goods enter Nigeria
options.c: Countries outside Nigeria to which free zone entities export
options.d: The part of Nigeria outside the free zones, under normal customs and tax rules

questions.explanation: The customs territory is the rest of Nigeria outside the zones; sales into it are treated as domestic sales. Option C describes export markets, and Option A is the zone itself, where the entity operates.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Lekki Zone Manufacturing Ltd, a licensed free zone entity, sells 35% of its output into the Nigerian customs territory in 2026. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what is the tax effect?

options.a: Its profits in respect of sales to the customs territory become taxable in Nigeria
options.b: It loses its licence and is wound up
options.c: Only 10% of its profits are taxable
options.d: It remains fully exempt because it is licensed in a free zone

questions.explanation: Once more than 25% of a free zone entity's sales go to the customs territory, tax accrues on its profits in respect of those customs-territory sales. Option D ignores the 25% limit, and Option B confuses a tax consequence with licensing.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, from what date will a free zone entity's profits from sales to the customs territory be fully taxable, whatever the percentage of such sales?

options.a: 26 June 2025, when the Act was signed
options.c: 1 January 2028, unless extended by Presidential order

questions.explanation: From 1 January 2028, profits from sales to the customs territory become fully taxable regardless of the 25% threshold, unless the date is extended by Presidential order. Option B is the commencement date of the Act, when the 25% rule starts.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the President may extend the 1 January 2028 date for taxing free zone entities' customs-territory sales for up to how long?

options.a: Up to 10 years from the commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025
options.c: Up to 25 years from the entity's licence date

questions.explanation: The President may, by order, extend the date for up to 10 years from the commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. Option B ignores the statutory limit, and Option C confuses the 25% sales threshold with a time period.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In 2028, with no Presidential extension in force, a free zone entity sells 10% of its output to the customs territory. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how are profits from those sales treated?

options.a: Only half of those profits are taxable
options.b: They are taxable, because from 2028 customs-territory sales are taxable whatever the percentage
options.c: They are exempt, because 10% is below the 25% threshold
options.d: They are exempt, because free zone entities are never taxed

questions.explanation: From 1 January 2028, the 25% safe harbour falls away, so profits from any level of sales into the customs territory are taxable. Option C applies the pre-2028 rule.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In 2026 a licensed free zone entity has total sales of N600,000,000, of which N120,000,000 are to the Nigerian customs territory and the rest are exports. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what percentage of its sales goes to the customs territory, and is it fully exempt?

options.d: 80%; fully exempt only if it pays a levy

questions.explanation: Customs-territory share = N120,000,000 / N600,000,000 = 20%, which is not more than 25%, so the entity is fully exempt in 2026. Option A divides by export sales instead of total sales, giving 25%.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In 2026 a free zone entity has total sales of N800,000,000, including N280,000,000 to the customs territory. Its profit on those customs-territory sales is N60,000,000. With companies income tax at 30% under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (the entity is not a small company), what tax is payable?

options.c: Nil, because the entity is in a free zone

questions.explanation: Share = N280,000,000/N800,000,000 = 35%, above 25%, so profits on customs-territory sales are taxable: 30% x N60,000,000 = N18,000,000. Option C ignores the 25% limit, and Option A wrongly scales the profit a second time.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In 2027 a free zone entity sells N100,000,000 to the customs territory out of total sales of N400,000,000. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what is its position?

options.a: 75% of sales; fully exempt as an exporter
options.b: 25% of sales; fully exempt, as the share is not more than 25%
options.c: 25% of sales; taxable, because the limit is less than 25%
options.d: 33% of sales; taxable on customs-territory sales

questions.explanation: Share = N100,000,000/N400,000,000 = 25%. The exemption holds where sales to the customs territory are not more than 25%, so exactly 25% is still exempt in 2027. Option D divides by export sales (N300,000,000), and Option A gives the export share instead.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In 2026 a free zone entity makes total profit of N200,000,000. 40% of its sales are to the customs territory, and profit is earned evenly across all sales. With companies income tax at 30% under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what tax is payable?
questions.explanation: 40% exceeds 25%, so profits on customs-territory sales are taxable: 40% x N200,000,000 = N80,000,000; tax = 30% = N24,000,000. Option D taxes all profits including exports, and Option A taxes only the excess over 25%.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In 2028 (no Presidential extension) a free zone entity sells 10% of its output in the customs territory, earning a profit of N20,000,000 on those sales. With companies income tax at 30% under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what tax is due on those profits?
questions.explanation: From 1 January 2028, customs-territory sales are taxable regardless of percentage: 30% x N20,000,000 = N6,000,000. Option C applies the pre-2028 25% safe harbour, and Option D multiplies by the 10% share even though N20,000,000 is already the profit on those sales.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Which non-tax privileges continue for free zone entities after the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 removed their blanket tax exemption?

options.a: Exemption from filing any tax returns
options.b: Privileges such as 100% foreign ownership and repatriation of profits
options.c: Freedom to sell any amount in the customs territory tax-free
options.d: Exemption from registering with the Nigeria Revenue Service

questions.explanation: The blanket tax exemption provisions of the zone laws were repealed, but non-fiscal privileges such as 100% foreign ownership and profit repatriation remain. Options A and D are wrong because free zone entities must still register and file returns, and Option C ignores the 25% limit.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Which of the following statements about free zone entities under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 is NOT correct?

options.a: A free zone entity remains fully exempt however much it sells in the customs territory
options.b: Profits are fully exempt where sales are wholly exports or inputs for exports
options.c: Sales to the customs territory above 25% make the related profits taxable
options.d: From 1 January 2028, customs-territory sales become taxable regardless of percentage, unless extended

questions.explanation: The exemption is limited: above 25% of sales to the customs territory, the related profits are taxable, and from 2028 any such sales are taxable. Options B, C and D correctly describe the rules.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the Economic Development Tax Incentive replaces which earlier incentive?
questions.explanation: The Economic Development Tax Incentive replaces the Pioneer Status Incentive, which was granted under the repealed Industrial Development (Income Tax Relief) Act. Option A is a separate regime that continues in a modified form.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: How does the Economic Development Tax Incentive under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 differ from the old Pioneer Status Incentive?

options.a: It gives a tax credit based on qualifying capital expenditure instead of a blanket tax holiday
options.b: It exempts all dividends of the company permanently
options.c: It applies only to companies outside Nigeria
options.d: It gives a longer blanket tax holiday of 10 years

questions.explanation: Pioneer status gave a full tax holiday, whereas the Economic Development Tax Incentive gives an economic development tax credit linked to qualifying capital expenditure. Option D describes a blanket exemption, which the new regime moves away from.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, who may apply for an economic development incentive certificate?

options.a: A Nigerian-incorporated company, or promoters of a proposed company, meeting the QCE threshold
options.b: Any foreign company exporting goods to Nigeria, whatever its investment
options.c: Any individual sole trader operating in a priority sector
options.d: Only companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange with a priority product

questions.explanation: Applications may be made by a company incorporated in Nigeria (including promoters of a company not yet incorporated) whose qualifying capital expenditure on or before production day meets the threshold. Options B and C fall outside the eligible applicants, and Option D adds a listing condition that does not exist.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, where are the minimum qualifying capital expenditure thresholds for each priority sector set out?

options.a: In the Second Schedule to the Act
options.b: In the Tenth Schedule to the Act
options.c: In the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023
options.d: In the First Schedule to the Act

questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule lists the priority sectors and the qualifying capital expenditure each must reach on or before production day. Option D contains the capital allowance rules, and Option A contains the free zone rules.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: To which body is an application for an economic development incentive certificate made under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, and who finally approves it?

options.a: Application to the Nigeria Revenue Service; approval by the Joint Revenue Board
options.b: Application to the Nigeria Customs Service; approval by the Minister of Trade
options.c: Application to the Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission (NIPC); approval by the President
options.d: Application to the Corporate Affairs Commission; approval by the National Assembly

questions.explanation: The application goes to the NIPC, which recommends it through the Minister to the President for approval. Option A names the tax collector and coordinating board, which do not grant the certificate.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, once the President approves an existing company's application for an economic development incentive certificate, within what time must the NIPC issue the certificate?
questions.explanation: The NIPC must issue the certificate and notify the applicant within 30 days of the President's approval. Option C confuses this with the three-month period for incorporating a proposed company.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how long is the initial economic development incentive period, and when does it start?

options.a: Ten years, starting from the date of application
options.b: Five years, starting from the company's production day
options.c: Three years, starting from the date of incorporation
options.d: Five years, starting from 1 January 2026 for all companies

questions.explanation: The incentive period is five years and commences on the production day of the company. Option C uses the old pioneer-style three-year period and the wrong start date, and Option D wrongly ties every company to the Act's commencement.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, on what condition can the initial five-year economic development incentive period be extended for another five years?

options.a: If the company pays an extension fee of 0.1% of its turnover
options.b: If the company exports at least 25% of its output each year
options.c: If the company reinvests 100% of its profits during the incentive period to expand the same product(s)
options.d: If the company employs more than 500 Nigerians during the period

questions.explanation: The period may be extended by a further five years where the company reinvests all of its profits to expand the same priority product line. Option A confuses the extension with the application fee, and Option B borrows the free zone 25% figure.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, at what rate is the economic development tax credit earned on qualifying capital expenditure?

options.a: 5% of qualifying capital expenditure per year for five years
options.c: 100% of qualifying capital expenditure in year one
options.d: 30% of qualifying capital expenditure in the first year only

questions.explanation: The incentive gives an annual tax credit of 5% of qualifying capital expenditure for five years. Option D confuses the credit with the companies income tax rate, and Option B uses turnover instead of capital expenditure.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Kogi Steel Ltd holds an economic development incentive certificate and incurred qualifying capital expenditure of N3,000,000,000. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (credit of 5% of QCE per year for five years), what is the annual economic development tax credit?
questions.explanation: Annual credit = 5% x N3,000,000,000 = N150,000,000. Option D is the total credit over five years, and Option B wrongly spreads the annual figure over five years again.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: A priority company incurred qualifying capital expenditure of N3,000,000,000. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (credit of 5% of QCE per year for five years), what is the total credit earned over the five-year period?
questions.explanation: Total credit = 5% x N3,000,000,000 x 5 = 25% x N3,000,000,000 = N750,000,000. Option A is one year's credit, and Option C assumes the full expenditure is credited.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: In year 1 of its incentive period a priority company earns an economic development tax credit of 5% of its N2,000,000,000 qualifying capital expenditure. Its tax payable on priority profits for the year is N60,000,000. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how much credit is left unused to carry forward?

options.c: Nil, because unused credit is lost immediately

questions.explanation: Credit = 5% x N2,000,000,000 = N100,000,000; used against tax payable N60,000,000; unused = N40,000,000. Option D forgets the credit used, and Option C ignores the carry-forward rule.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what happens to economic development tax credit that remains unused at the end of the priority period?

options.a: It lapses immediately at the end of the priority period
options.b: It may be used within five years after the priority period, after which any balance lapses
options.c: It is refunded in cash by the Nigeria Revenue Service
options.d: It can be carried forward indefinitely

questions.explanation: Unused credit can be utilised within five years of assessment after the priority period ends; anything still unused then lapses. Option C is wrong because the credit is not refundable in cash, and Option D ignores the five-year limit.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which liability can the economic development tax credit NOT be used to offset?

options.a: Tax payable in any year within the priority period
options.b: Companies income tax on profits from the priority product
options.c: Additional tax payable under the minimum effective tax rate rules
options.d: Tax on priority profits in the first year of the incentive period

questions.explanation: The credit offsets tax payable during the priority period but cannot reduce the additional (top-up) tax payable under the minimum effective tax rate rules. Options A, B and D are liabilities the credit is designed to offset.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what record-keeping duty applies to a company enjoying the Economic Development Tax Incentive?

options.a: It must file its accounts only with the NIPC and not with the tax authority
options.b: It must keep records only for its non-priority business
options.c: It need not keep any records during the incentive period
options.d: It must keep separate books and records for its priority and non-priority income

questions.explanation: A priority company must keep separate books for priority products and for other income, so the credit is applied only to priority profits. Option A is wrong because returns of profits are still required under the tax law.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, can a company enjoying the Economic Development Tax Incentive also claim other tax reliefs for the same activity?

options.a: Yes, provided it pays an extra 4% development levy
options.b: No, it is excluded from other tax reliefs while it enjoys the incentive
options.c: Yes, it can combine the incentive with any other relief
options.d: Yes, but only with the free trade zone exemption

questions.explanation: A company granted the certificate and enjoying the incentive is excluded from simultaneously enjoying other tax reliefs under the Act or any other law. Options C and D allow stacking of reliefs, which the exclusion rule prevents.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a priority sector eligible for the Economic Development Tax Incentive under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?
questions.explanation: Priority sectors include aquaculture, crude oil refining, electricity and gas supply, pharmaceuticals and chemicals, automobiles, renewable energy, medical equipment and textiles, among others. Options B, C and D are not among the listed productive priority sectors.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the priority sectors listed for the Economic Development Tax Incentive under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?
questions.explanation: The listed priority sectors are mainly productive and industrial activities such as renewable energy, textiles, automobiles, metal processing and medical equipment. Options A, B and D all appear in the list, while commercial banking does not.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: For an economic development incentive application, the NIPC charges a non-refundable fee of 0.1% of qualifying capital expenditure, capped at N5,000,000. What fee is payable on QCE of N2,000,000,000?
questions.explanation: Fee = 0.1% x N2,000,000,000 = N2,000,000, which is below the N5,000,000 cap. Option D applies the cap although it is not reached, and Option B uses 1% instead of 0.1%.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: For an economic development incentive application, the NIPC charges a non-refundable fee of 0.1% of qualifying capital expenditure, capped at N5,000,000. What fee is payable on QCE of N8,000,000,000?
questions.explanation: 0.1% x N8,000,000,000 = N8,000,000, which exceeds the cap, so the fee is limited to N5,000,000. Option B ignores the cap.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: What happens to a company that already held a pioneer status certificate when the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 commenced?

options.a: It keeps its pioneer relief for the unexpired period of the certificate
options.b: Its pioneer period is automatically doubled
options.c: It loses the relief immediately on 1 January 2026
options.d: It must repay all taxes previously exempted

questions.explanation: Existing pioneer status beneficiaries continue to enjoy the relief for the unexpired part of their period, while new applicants use the Economic Development Tax Incentive. Option C ignores the transition rule, and Option D has no legal basis.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, for how long is the income of a company engaged in an agricultural business (such as crop production, livestock, aquaculture, forestry or dairy) exempt from tax?

options.a: For the first five years from commencement of the business
options.c: For the first three years only
options.d: Permanently, as long as it remains in agriculture

questions.explanation: Agricultural businesses enjoy an income tax exemption for the first five years after they start business. Option C is too short, and Option D turns a time-limited relief into a permanent one.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Which of the following businesses is among those listed as enjoying the five-year agricultural tax exemption under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?

options.d: Processing of cocoa into cocoa butter, cocoa oil and chocolate

questions.explanation: The agricultural exemption extends to activities such as dairy production, cocoa processing and the manufacture of animal feeds. Options A, B and C are trading or service businesses, not the listed agricultural activities.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Oyo Dairy Ltd commenced business on 1 January 2026, producing pasteurised milk and cheese. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how is its 2028 income treated?

options.a: Exempt, because 2028 falls within its first five years of business
options.b: Taxable at 30%, because dairy is not an agricultural business
options.c: Taxable at 30%, because the exemption covers only the first two years
options.d: Exempt only if it exports all its products

questions.explanation: Dairy production is a listed agricultural business, and 2028 is the third year after commencement, inside the five-year exemption window. Option B wrongly excludes dairy, and Option D adds an export condition that the agricultural exemption does not contain.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Zaria Feeds Ltd, which manufactures animal feeds, commenced business on 1 January 2026. It is not a small company and has no other relief. Its 2031 taxable profit is N50,000,000. With companies income tax at 30% under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what tax is payable for 2031?
questions.explanation: The five-year exemption covers 2026 to 2030, so 2031 (the sixth year) is taxable: 30% x N50,000,000 = N15,000,000. Option B wrongly treats 2031 as within the exemption period.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the profits of a Nigerian company from goods exported from Nigeria are exempt from income tax on what condition?

options.a: The company pays VAT at 7.5% on the exports
options.b: The goods are exported to an ECOWAS country only
options.c: The export proceeds are repatriated to Nigeria through official channels
options.d: The company is located in a free trade zone

questions.explanation: Export profits are exempt where the proceeds are repatriated through official channels; petroleum operations are excluded from this exemption. Option D is wrong because the exemption is not limited to free zone entities, and Option A contradicts the zero-rating of exports.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Ada Ventures, a venture capital fund, sells shares in a labelled startup that it held in Nigeria for 30 months. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, how is the gain treated?

options.a: Exempt only if the startup is a manufacturing company in a free zone
options.b: Taxable, because the minimum holding period is 36 months
options.c: Taxable, because only angel investors qualify
options.d: Exempt, because the asset was held for at least 24 months

questions.explanation: Gains of angel investors, venture capitalists, private equity funds, accelerators and incubators on assets in labelled startups are exempt where the assets were held in Nigeria for at least 24 months. Option C wrongly excludes venture capitalists, and Option B invents a longer holding period.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: An angel investor sells her shares in a labelled startup after holding them in Nigeria for 18 months. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, does the startup gains exemption apply?

options.a: Yes, because all startup gains are exempt
options.b: No, because angel investors are excluded from the exemption
options.c: Yes, because the minimum holding period is 12 months
options.d: No, because the 24-month minimum holding period has not been met

questions.explanation: The exemption applies only where the startup assets have been held in Nigeria for at least 24 months, and 18 months falls short. Option C uses the wrong period, and Option B is wrong because angel investors are expressly covered.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, dividends received from investments in which type of business are exempt from income tax?

options.a: Businesses that pay the development levy
options.c: Businesses with turnover above N100 million

questions.explanation: The Act exempts dividends received from investments in wholly export-oriented businesses, to encourage investment in exporters. Options A, C and D describe features with no link to this exemption.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Enugu Agro Exports Ltd exports processed cashew nuts and brings the proceeds back to Nigeria through its bank via official foreign exchange channels. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, what is the likely tax position of its export profits?

options.a: Taxable at 15% under the minimum effective tax rate
options.b: Taxable at 30%, because only free zone entities can enjoy export exemptions
options.c: Exempt only for the first two years
options.d: Exempt from income tax, because the export proceeds were repatriated through official channels

questions.explanation: Profits from goods exported from Nigeria are exempt where the proceeds are repatriated through official channels, and the business is not a petroleum operation. Option B is wrong because this exemption is separate from the free zone regime.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: A company holding an economic development incentive certificate also runs a non-priority business. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the economic development tax credit is based on the tax payable on profits from:

options.b: The priority product or service during the priority period
options.d: All the company's businesses, priority and non-priority

questions.explanation: The credit relates to tax on profits from the priority product or service earned in the priority period, which is why separate records must be kept. Option D would extend the incentive to non-priority income, which the Act does not allow.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: A priority company earns an economic development tax credit of 5% of its N1,000,000,000 qualifying capital expenditure each year. Its tax payable on priority profits in years 1, 2 and 3 is N20,000,000, N40,000,000 and N70,000,000. If unused credit is carried forward and used in later years of the priority period, what unused credit remains at the end of year 3?
questions.explanation: Each year's credit is N50,000,000, so 3 years = N150,000,000; total tax offset = N130,000,000; unused = N150,000,000 - N130,000,000 = N20,000,000. Option B forgets to use credit against year 3 tax, and Option C looks at year 1 only.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Which statement best compares the free trade zone regime with the Economic Development Tax Incentive under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?

options.a: Both depend only on the number of Nigerian employees
options.b: Free zone relief turns on where sales go; the incentive turns on QCE in a priority sector
options.c: Both are granted and administered by the Nigeria Customs Service
options.d: Free zone relief is a 5% tax credit, while the incentive is a full exemption

questions.explanation: Free zone entities are exempt according to how much they sell to the customs territory, while the incentive gives a credit tied to qualifying capital expenditure by an approved priority company. Option D reverses the two mechanisms.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Which condition must a priority company meet regarding its qualifying capital expenditure to be considered for an economic development incentive certificate under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025?

options.a: Its capital expenditure must be below N250 million
options.b: The qualifying capital expenditure incurred on or before production day must not be below the threshold for its sector
options.c: It must have incurred no capital expenditure before production day
options.d: Its capital expenditure must be financed only with foreign loans

questions.explanation: An application is considered only where the qualifying capital expenditure incurred on or before production day is at least the amount set for its sector in the Tenth Schedule. Option A turns a minimum threshold into a maximum.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Apapa Free Zone Packaging Ltd, a licensed free zone entity, pays a Lagos consulting firm for management services. Under the 2025 framework, is the payment automatically free of withholding tax because the payer is in a free zone?

options.a: No, and the free zone entity also loses its income tax exemption
options.b: Yes, all payments by or to free zone entities are outside withholding tax
options.c: No, free zone entities have no general withholding tax exemption, so deduction rules still apply
options.d: Yes, but only if the consultant is also in a free zone

questions.explanation: The 2025 framework gives free zone entities no general withholding tax exemption, so payments such as management or professional fees remain subject to the deduction rules. Option B overstates the free zone privileges, and Option A wrongly links a withholding duty to the entity's own income tax position.

questions.topic: Tax Incentives and Free Trade Zones
questions.question: Ijebu Glass Ltd holds an economic development incentive certificate and its production day is 1 July 2026. Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the initial incentive period is five years from production day, extendable by five more years if 100% of profits are reinvested in the same product(s). If no extension is granted, on what date does the initial incentive period end?
questions.explanation: Five years running from 1 July 2026 end on 30 June 2031. Option A counts only four years, Option C wrongly runs the period from 1 January 2026, and Option D assumes the five-year extension was granted.
